title: BitNet b1.58 and 1-Bit LLMs: Replacing Floating-Point Matrix Multiplications with Integer Addition
summary: High-bandwidth memory bandwidth and energy-hungry matrix multiplication (GEMM) units represent the two primary physical bottlenecks in modern LLM inference. BitNet b1.58 introduces a radical architectural shift: constraining every parameter in the linear projection layers to a ternary set {-1, 0, 1}. Because multiplying any number by -1, 0, or 1 requires only sign inversion or zeroing, 1.58-bit models replace expensive floating-point multiplications entirely with integer addition. This unlocks order-of-magnitude energy savings and allows massive LLMs to run at high speed on cost-effective CPU and edge silicon.
analogyTitle: The Real-Life Analogy: The Precision Scientific Calculator vs. The Three-Position Light Switch
analogy:
Imagine calculating the final bill for a massive catering order.

Under Standard Floating-Point LLMs (FP16/BF16), every single item price has 16 digits of decimal precision (e.g., $14.39841). Calculating the total requires a powerful scientific calculator constantly performing high-precision multiplication, heating up the device and consuming substantial battery power.

Under BitNet b1.58 (The Three-Position Light Switch), every ingredient is simplified into a three-position mechanical toggle: 'Add it' (+1), 'Leave it out' (0), or 'Deduct it' (-1). Instead of performing multiplication, the accountant simply walks down the list pressing add or subtract buttons. The final flavor profile matches the original recipe, but the mental calculation takes 90% less time and uses almost zero battery.

sections.heading: 1. The Physics of Matrix Multiplications: Why FP16 Burns Power
sections.content:
In standard transformer architectures, the feed-forward networks (FFN) and attention projection layers rely on General Matrix Multiply (GEMM) kernels: Y = W • X. Multiplying FP16 or FP8 numbers requires dedicated Tensor Cores with complex multi-stage mantissa aligners and exponent adders.

• Energy Disparity: On modern silicon, a 16-bit floating-point multiplication (FP16 MUL) consumes roughly 1.1 picojoules (pJ), whereas a 16-bit integer addition (INT ADD) consumes just 0.1 pJ. Standard inference spends 90% of its electrical power doing floating-point arithmetic inside matrix engines.
• Memory Footprint: Storing 70 billion parameters in FP16 demands 140 GB of ultra-expensive High Bandwidth Memory (HBM3e), requiring multi-GPU partitioning just to hold model weights.

sections.heading: 2. Inside BitNet b1.58: Ternary Weight Quantization
sections.content:
BitNet b1.58 represents weights as ternary values from {-1, 0, 1}, meaning each weight requires log2(3) ≈ 1.58 bits of entropy:

• Absmean Weight Quantization: Weights are scaled by the mean absolute value of the weight matrix and rounded to the nearest integer in {-1, 0, 1}:
W_quant = Clip(Round(W / γ), -1, 1) where γ = (1/nm) ∑ |W_ij|.
• 8-Bit Activation Quantization: Unlike weights, dynamic token activations retain higher precision (INT8) using per-token absolute maximum scaling (absmax).
• Multiplication-Free GEMM: When computing Y = W_quant • X_quant, the hardware never multiplies. For each element in X, if W is 1, it adds X; if W is -1, it subtracts X; if W is 0, it skips it. The GEMM kernel reduces to a pure integer addition accumulator.

sections.heading: 3. Hardware Implications: The Future of Edge and CPU Serving
sections.content:
Eliminating multiplications unlocks unprecedented hardware democratization:

• CPU and SRAM Viability: Without requiring specialized Tensor Cores, BitNet models achieve GPU-level token-per-second generation speeds on standard consumer CPUs and low-power NPUs.
• Slashing SRAM Caching Overhead: Because weights are 85% smaller than FP16 baselines, large chunks of model weights can reside directly in ultra-fast L2/L3 cache or on-chip SRAM, bypassing external DRAM buses and cutting memory-bound latency by up to 4x.

takeaway: Traditional neural networks consume massive energy multiplying high-precision floating-point numbers. BitNet b1.58 quantizes weights to {-1, 0, 1}, replacing matrix multiplication with simple integer addition. This reduces memory footprint by up to 85%, slashes arithmetic energy by 90%, and makes frontier-grade LLM inference viable on cost-effective CPU and edge hardware.
